title: Ada-K Routing: Boosting the Efficiency of MoE-based LLMs

contributions.purpose: Improve the efficiency/performance balance of MoE-based LLMs, whose conventional static Top-K routing activates a fixed equal number of experts per token regardless of token importance.
contributions.mechanism: Ada-K routing: a dynamic per-token strategy that adjusts the number of activated experts. A pluggable, lightweight learnable allocator module outputs a distribution over expert counts and samples the count for each token, replacing fixed Top-K.
contributions.evaluation: Vs Top-K across four MoE-based LLMs (14.3B to 140B params): reduces activated experts by 30-40%, over 25% FLOPs reduction, over 20% inference speedup, while improving performance across benchmarks.
contributions.source_quote: We propose a dynamic Ada-K routing strategy that adjusts the activated experts number on a per-token basis to enhance the conventional Top-K routing. Compared to Top-K routing, Ada-K routing manages to save over 25% FLOPs and achieve more than 20% acceleration in inference, while enhancing performance.

contributions.purpose: Train the allocator despite the expert-count sampling operation being non-differentiable, and keep training cheap.
contributions.mechanism: An RL-based end-to-end training framework using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) to optimize the lightweight allocator modules for the non-differentiable decision-making of expert allocation.
contributions.evaluation: Highly training-efficient: only ~2M tunable parameters; training under 8 hours for all baselines, including Mixtral-8x22B (>140B params).
contributions.source_quote: We introduce a learnable and lightweight allocator module that determines the optimal number of activated experts for each token through end-to-end training. Reinforcement learning techniques have been carefully designed and introduced to facilitate the training of this non-differentiable decision-making framework.

contributions.purpose: Understand and validate what drives adaptive expert allocation, providing design insights.
contributions.mechanism: Detailed quantitative and qualitative analysis of Ada-K allocation at the task, layer, and token levels across four MoE LLMs.
contributions.evaluation: Consistent advantages over baselines; analysis finds harder tasks, middle layers, and content words tend to activate more experts.
contributions.domain: Efficient MoE LLM inference / interpretability of routing
contributions.source_quote: We extensively evaluate our method across four popular MoE-based LLMs, ranging from 14.3B to 140B parameters. Ada-K routing demonstrates consistent advantages over these baselines. The effectiveness of our proposed method is further validated by extensive qualitative analyses.

self_declared_provenance.quote: The most common routing strategy is Top-K routing (Shazeer et al., 2017b). ... In our study, we introduce a parameter-efficient and data-efficient training framework that introduces lightweight learnable modules, i.e. allocators. These allocators seamlessly work with routers to dynamically assign expert resources across individual tokens.

we employ the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm (Stiennon et al., 2020; Nakano et al., 2021) to optimize the allocators end-to-end, towards ideal balance between model performance and efficiency.

notes: Positive results throughout; the method is framed as strictly improving on Top-K (both efficiency and performance). Note the two headline efficiency numbers are stated slightly differently in abstract vs contributions (abstract: 30-40% fewer activated experts / >25% FLOPs / >20% speedup). No negative or trade-off result reported for the proposed method.
